events.what: Karimullah, 'Solution of Brocard's Problem', Indian Journal of Advanced Mathematics, claims a full proof that n = 4, 5, 7 are the only solutions
events.credibility_reason: F5: claims to settle a landmark problem open for about 150 years; no citation, discussion or expert uptake in over two years; APC-funded venue with no evidence of indexing; later literature (erdosproblems.com entry, Naciri 2025, Bravo 2026) treats the problem as open and does not cite it.

events.what: Makki Naciri proves n = 4, 5, 7 are the only solutions when x±1 is 7-free, and finiteness when x±1 is k-free or a prime power
Bravo shows (4,5) is the only solution with x a Padovan or Perrin number
Takeda resolves the polynomial analogue over F_q[T]

judgement.doubts: Naciri's restriction is on the solution x (x±1 7-free), a genuine case of the stated equation. Only the Zenodo page and erdosproblems.com summary were read, not the Integers paper; Integers publication taken from the record. Takeda's date is the online publication date, the first preprint date is not in the record. Karimullah set aside as not_credible, though the record could not read its PDF.
